ports.name: clk
ports.desc: Synchronous core clock; divided down to generate MDC (≤2.5 MHz, IEEE 802.3 §8).

ports.name: rst_n
ports.desc: Active-low synchronous reset. MDIO has no dedicated reset wire on the bus (IEEE 802.3 §11); this is the chip's own reset.

ports.name: start
ports.desc: Pulse high for one clk to launch a management frame.

ports.name: phyad
ports.desc: PHYAD (Clause 22) / PRTAD (Clause 45), selects one of 32 PHYs/ports (IEEE 802.3 §3/§5/§9).

ports.name: wdata
ports.desc: 16-bit write data, or the register address payload on a Clause 45 Address frame (IEEE 802.3 §3/§5).

ports.name: rdata
ports.desc: 16-bit data captured from the PHY on a read frame (IEEE 802.3 §3).

ports.name: busy
ports.desc: High while a management frame is in flight.

ports.name: done
ports.desc: One-clk pulse when a frame completes.

ports.name: rd_valid
ports.desc: Asserted with done when the completed frame was a read.

ports.name: mdc
ports.desc: Management Data Clock, sourced by the STA, ≤2.5 MHz; PHY/MMD samples MDIO on its rising edge (IEEE 802.3 §2).

ports.name: mdio_o
ports.desc: MDIO drive value to the pad (open-drain line; STA-driven in the command portion) (IEEE 802.3 §2/§7).

ports.name: mdio_oe
ports.desc: MDIO output-enable to the pad (1 = STA drives; released to Hi-Z during read turnaround so the PHY can drive) (IEEE 802.3 §7).

ports.name: mdio_i
ports.desc: MDIO sampled value from the pad (PHY-driven in the read-data portion) (IEEE 802.3 §2/§7).

fsm_states.name: IDLE
fsm_states.desc: MDIO released (Hi-Z, pulled high); wait for a STA-issued transaction.

fsm_states.name: PRE
fsm_states.desc: Drive/skip the 32-bit preamble (32 contiguous ones; mdc_cnt counts the 32 MDC cycles).

fsm_states.name: HDR
fsm_states.desc: Shift the 14-bit command header ST(2)+OP(2)+PHYAD/PRTAD(5)+REGAD/DEVAD(5) MSB-first out of cmd_sr.

fsm_states.name: TA
fsm_states.desc: 2-bit turnaround: drive 10 on a write; on a read tri-state MDIO in bit 1 then sample PHY-driven 0 in bit 2 (Z0).

fsm_states.name: DATA
fsm_states.desc: Shift the 16-bit DATA field MSB-first through data_sr: drive on write, sample on read.

fsm_states.name: DONE
fsm_states.desc: Last data bit clocked; release MDIO (Hi-Z) and signal transaction complete.

internal_wires.name: mdc_cnt
internal_wires.desc: MDC bit counter: counts the 32 preamble cycles and the per-field bit positions.

internal_wires.name: cmd_sr
internal_wires.desc: Command-header shift register holding ST+OP+PHYAD+REGAD, shifted MSB first.

internal_wires.name: data_sr
internal_wires.desc: 16-bit DATA shift register, MSB first (drive on write, capture on read).

derived_from_L2.protocol_overview.label: verdict_byte_offset defaulted to 6 (AID-class half-duplex single-wire convention) — L3 did not extract an offset
expected_verdict_byte_hex defaulted to AID-class protocol PASS sentinel (canonical 0xF2 at byte_offset 6); L3 did not extract a verdict-byte literal — low_confidence

module_role: Synchronous serial peripheral block within an MCU; couples to MCU bus on one side (8-bit register file at module-defined offsets) and to 4 external pins on the other.

integration_overview.master: Station Management entity (STA), typically embedded in the MAC
integration_overview.topology: single STA, shared MDC and MDIO, up to 32 PHYs/ports selected by 5-bit PHYAD/PRTAD
integration_overview.init_sequence: No dedicated reset wire; STA reads Status (Reg 1) and PHY ID (Reg 2/3) to discover the PHY, then configures auto-negotiation via BMCR (Reg 0) and the auto-negotiation registers.

interface_categories: Bidirectional mode (single data pin via SPC0=1)
interconnect_topologies_supported: Point-to-point: one master + one slave (3-wire MOSI/MISO/SCK + optional SS)
Multi-slave: one master + multiple slaves (independent SS per slave)
Multi-master: multiple masters sharing MOSI/MISO/SCK with mode-fault arbitration
default_signal_values_when_omitted: See L4 register reset values. SPE=0 after reset disables the module and tri-states/idles all pins.

wait_mode.SPISWAI_1: SPI clock stopped; master aborts in-progress transmission until CPU re-enters run mode; slave continues if master still drives SCK.

low_power_modes.stop_mode: SPI inactive; master aborts in-progress transmission; slave continues if master still drives SCK.

spi_run_mode_when_SPE_clear: Module clock to SPI core gated off; register access still permitted.
soc_dependent_items: Pin pad drive strength and slew
Max allowed baud rate (per SoC SPI Electrical Specification)
default_signal_values_when_idle: SDA = HIGH, SCL = HIGH (both released, pulled up by Rp). The bus is 'free' after tBUF following a STOP condition.
bus_clear_procedure: If SDA stuck LOW: master sends 9 SCL clock pulses to allow the device holding SDA LOW to release it. If SCL stuck LOW: use HW reset pin or cycle power.

daisy_chain_rules.TDO_to_TDI_handoff: TDO of device N is wired directly to TDI of device N+1.
daisy_chain_rules.shared_TCK_TMS: TCK and TMS are bussed to all devices; FSMs in all devices step in lockstep.
daisy_chain_rules.total_scan_length: Sum of the widths of the selected register in each device. To shift a single DR through one device, all other devices must be in BYPASS (1 bit each).
daisy_chain_rules.instruction_loading: To load distinct instructions into different devices, the tester scans a concatenated IR with each device's IR opcode in the correct slot.

compatibility_notes: BSDL files are the integration-time contract describing a device's pin assignments and BSR cell types.
HSDL and SVF standardize vector exchange between EDA tools.
JTAG bus may be reused at runtime for emulation / programming / configuration (e.g. ARM JTAG-DP, Altera/Xilinx FPGA configuration).
topology_description: Each MAC is connected to exactly one PHY via a single MII / GMII / RGMII / XGMII data path. The PHY's MDI side connects to one network medium (twisted pair / fiber). At the network level, every modern Ethernet link is point-to-point and full-duplex behind a switch; legacy CSMA/CD shared-medium half-duplex topologies (repeater hubs, coax) remain spec-compliant but are deprecated.
device_classes_examples: Standalone PHY chip (e.g. 100BASE-TX or 1000BASE-T transceiver behind MII / GMII / RGMII).
Multi-port Switch ASIC — N MACs + N PHYs + a per-port FIFO + a forwarding engine; each external port is one Ethernet link.
Network Interface Controller (NIC) — MAC + PHY + DMA engine + host bus interface (PCIe).
Industrial-Ethernet PHY (TPS-1 / PROFINET / EtherCAT) — same MAC + RS + MII + MDIO; added IRT scheduling at MAC client.
Automotive Ethernet PHY (100BASE-T1 / 1000BASE-T1) — single-pair full-duplex; same MAC + MII; PMD differs.
